englishGrammar.rule: 理解轉折信號詞 (but, however) 表達對比與轉折
englishGrammar.wrong: Zoos in the WZCS select list were carefully inspected.
englishGrammar.correct: Zoos in the WZCS select list were NOT carefully inspected.
englishGrammar.explanation: 轉折詞 'but' 表示實際情況與預期相反。句子前半段提出一種假設，但 'but' 之後的內容揭示了事實並非如此，因此前半段的判斷是錯誤的。

englishGrammar.rule: 理解讓步信號詞 (nevertheless, although) 表達讓步與重點
englishGrammar.wrong: The fall in profits was not disappointing because it was not unexpected.
englishGrammar.correct: Although the fall in profits was not unexpected, it is nevertheless very disappointing.
englishGrammar.explanation: 讓步詞 'nevertheless' 表示儘管某事不令人意外，但其結果仍然令人失望，強調後者的重要性。

englishGrammar.rule: 理解動詞詞組 'bring about' 表示因果關係
englishGrammar.wrong: Increased air temperature merely coincided with higher sea levels.
englishGrammar.correct: Increased air temperature brought about higher sea levels (i.e., caused higher sea levels).
englishGrammar.explanation: 'bring about' 是明確表示「導致」、「造成」因果關係的動詞詞組，而非僅僅是伴隨發生。

englishGrammar.wrong: tieing
englishGrammar.correct: tying
englishGrammar.explanation: 以-ie結尾的動詞，變為現在分詞（-ing形式）時，應將-ie改為-y再加-ing。
動詞形式需根據其前方主詞的單數或複數形式來決定。

englishGrammar.correct: 某人 and 某人 do something
englishGrammar.explanation: 當主詞為複數形式（如'某人 and 某人'）時，在現在簡單式中動詞應使用原型（base form）。

englishGrammar.wrong: I drink a sip of water.
englishGrammar.correct: I took a sip of water.
englishGrammar.explanation: 描述剛完成動作應使用過去式，且搭配詞為 take a sip。

englishGrammar.wrong: Outside has a big rainy.
englishGrammar.correct: It is raining heavily outside.
englishGrammar.explanation: Rainy 是形容詞，不能當名詞。描述下雨應使用 It is raining + 副詞。

englishGrammar.wrong: Where are you stay?
englishGrammar.correct: Where are you staying?
englishGrammar.explanation: 詢問目前居住狀態應使用 be + V-ing。

englishGrammar.wrong: We have many strong earthquake every year.
englishGrammar.correct: We have many strong earthquakes every year.
englishGrammar.explanation: Many 後面需接可數名詞複數。

englishGrammar.wrong: Today is weekend.
englishGrammar.correct: Today is the weekend.
englishGrammar.explanation: 表示本週週末時需加上定冠詞 the。

englishGrammar.wrong: I buy something, and it is very expensive.
englishGrammar.correct: I bought something, and it was very expensive.
englishGrammar.explanation: 描述過去發生的事，整句時態應一致。

englishGrammar.wrong: This one is more better.
englishGrammar.correct: This one is better.
englishGrammar.explanation: Better 本身即為比較級，前面不可加 more。

englishGrammar.wrong: I decide to have the exam in November 21.
englishGrammar.correct: I decided to take the exam on November 21.
englishGrammar.explanation: 考試用 take，特定日期前介系詞用 on。

englishGrammar.wrong: I maybe have four months to prepare.
englishGrammar.correct: I may have four months to prepare.
englishGrammar.explanation: Maybe 是副詞，May 才是情態動詞，可接原形動詞。

englishGrammar.wrong: Taiwan is have many typhoons.
englishGrammar.correct: Taiwan has many typhoons.
englishGrammar.explanation: 一般現在式直接用動詞即可，不需要 be 動詞。

englishGrammar.wrong: Everywhere has a lot of water.
englishGrammar.correct: There is water everywhere.
englishGrammar.explanation: 表示某處存在某物時，使用 there be 句型更自然。

englishGrammar.wrong: I spent twelve hours to fly to Seattle.
englishGrammar.correct: I spent twelve hours flying to Seattle.
englishGrammar.explanation: Spend time 後面應接 V-ing。

englishGrammar.wrong: I felt very tired.
englishGrammar.correct: The flight was very tiring, so I felt tired.
englishGrammar.explanation: 人感到的狀態用 -ed，造成狀態的事物用 -ing。

englishGrammar.wrong: Why do you laughing?
englishGrammar.correct: Why are you laughing?
englishGrammar.explanation: 正在笑是當下發生的動作，問句結構為 be＋主詞＋V-ing。

englishGrammar.rule: 事實描述用現在簡單式
englishGrammar.wrong: The River Nile is flowing into the Mediterranean.
englishGrammar.correct: The River Nile flows into the Mediterranean.
englishGrammar.explanation: 描述河流流向這項長期事實，使用現在簡單式。

englishGrammar.rule: 暫時狀況用現在進行式
englishGrammar.wrong: The river flows very fast today.
englishGrammar.correct: The river is flowing very fast today.
englishGrammar.explanation: 句子描述今天的特殊情況，而不是河流平常的狀態。

englishGrammar.wrong: More and more people use electric cars.
englishGrammar.correct: More and more people are using electric cars.
englishGrammar.explanation: more and more 表示正在增加，強調持續發展的趨勢。

englishGrammar.wrong: What does he went?
englishGrammar.correct: What does he want?
englishGrammar.explanation: does 後面必須使用動詞原形。

englishGrammar.wrong: I’m not believing it.
englishGrammar.correct: I don’t believe it.
englishGrammar.explanation: believe 表示內心相信的狀態，通常不用現在進行式。

englishGrammar.rule: be 與 be being 的區別
englishGrammar.wrong: Are you being hungry?
englishGrammar.correct: Are you hungry?
englishGrammar.explanation: hungry 是身體狀態，不能使用 being。

englishGrammar.rule: 未來安排使用現在進行式
englishGrammar.wrong: I go to Korea in August.
englishGrammar.correct: I’m going to Korea in August.
englishGrammar.explanation: 已經安排好的未來行程，可使用現在進行式。

englishGrammar.wrong: If you apply that three…
englishGrammar.correct: If you apply for three days of annual leave…
englishGrammar.explanation: 申請某物使用 apply for。

englishGrammar.rule: 現在完成式表達持續年資
englishGrammar.wrong: Because I already do this work three years.
englishGrammar.correct: Because I have worked here for three years.
englishGrammar.explanation: 從過去持續到現在的工作年資，使用 have worked + for。

englishGrammar.wrong: Our company is more than the lawyer.
englishGrammar.correct: Our company gives us more annual leave than the law requires.
englishGrammar.explanation: lawyer 是律師，law 才是法律。

englishGrammar.wrong: You can easy to communicate
englishGrammar.correct: You can communicate easily
englishGrammar.explanation: easy 是形容詞，修飾動詞 communicate 需使用副詞 easily。

englishGrammar.wrong: I will be exciting.
englishGrammar.correct: I will be excited.
englishGrammar.explanation: 描述人感到情緒使用 -ed 形容詞。

englishGrammar.wrong: teach → teached
englishGrammar.correct: teach → taught
englishGrammar.explanation: teach的過去式與過去分詞都是taught。

englishGrammar.wrong: fall → falled
englishGrammar.correct: fall → fell
englishGrammar.explanation: fall的過去式是fell，過去分詞是fallen。

englishGrammar.wrong: throw → throwed
englishGrammar.correct: throw → threw
englishGrammar.explanation: throw的過去式是threw，過去分詞是thrown。

englishGrammar.wrong: catch → catched
englishGrammar.correct: catch → caught
englishGrammar.explanation: catch的過去式與過去分詞都是caught。

englishGrammar.wrong: fly → flyed
englishGrammar.correct: fly → flew
englishGrammar.explanation: fly的過去式是flew，過去分詞是flown。

englishGrammar.wrong: How long did they take?
englishGrammar.correct: How long did it take?
englishGrammar.explanation: it代表該趟行程，也可以用How long did the journey take?

englishGrammar.wrong: How did the weather?
englishGrammar.correct: How was the weather?
englishGrammar.explanation: weather在描述狀態時使用be動詞，不使用did。

englishGrammar.wrong: My father taught me for driving car.
englishGrammar.correct: My father taught me to drive.
englishGrammar.explanation: 應使用teach someone to do something。

englishGrammar.wrong: I spent three hours to work.
englishGrammar.correct: I spent three hours working.
englishGrammar.explanation: spend＋時間＋V-ing。

englishGrammar.wrong: After worked off
englishGrammar.correct: After work
englishGrammar.explanation: after work 為固定用法，表示下班後。

englishGrammar.rule: irrespective of whether + 主詞 + 動詞
englishGrammar.wrong: Irrespective whether the method is formal or informal, the result remains the same.
englishGrammar.correct: Irrespective of whether the method is formal or informal, the result remains the same.
englishGrammar.explanation: irrespective 後方通常接 of；irrespective of whether 表示「不論是否……」。

englishGrammar.rule: find it + 形容詞 + to V
englishGrammar.wrong: Some students find easier to understand classroom language.
englishGrammar.correct: Some students find it easier to understand classroom language.
englishGrammar.explanation: 使用虛受詞 it 代替後方的 to understand classroom language。

englishGrammar.wrong: Despite the product was expensive, it remained popular.
englishGrammar.correct: Despite its high price, the product remained popular.
englishGrammar.explanation: despite 後方不能直接接完整子句。若要接完整子句，可改用 although。

englishGrammar.rule: one of the + 最高級 + 複數名詞
englishGrammar.wrong: Sydney Harbour is one of the largest port in the world.
englishGrammar.correct: Sydney Harbour is one of the largest ports in the world.
englishGrammar.explanation: one of the 後方表示「多個之中的一個」，因此名詞必須使用複數。

englishGrammar.rule: has或have yet to + 原形動詞
englishGrammar.wrong: The government has yet introduced a ban.
englishGrammar.correct: The government has yet to introduce a ban.
englishGrammar.explanation: has yet to do 表示「尚未做某事」，yet 後方必須接 to 加原形動詞。

englishGrammar.rule: neither A nor B 的動詞通常配合較接近的主詞
englishGrammar.wrong: Neither the managers nor the workers trusts the new system.
englishGrammar.correct: Neither the managers nor the workers trust the new system.
englishGrammar.explanation: 最接近動詞的主詞 workers 是複數，因此使用 trust。

englishGrammar.rule: be more similar to A than to B
englishGrammar.wrong: Classroom language is more similar with middle-class language than working-class language.
englishGrammar.correct: Classroom language is more similar to middle-class language than to working-class language.
englishGrammar.explanation: similar 通常搭配介系詞 to；完整比較可使用 more similar to A than to B。

englishGrammar.rule: 現在完成進行式（活動跡象）
englishGrammar.wrong: Have you worked hard?
englishGrammar.correct: Have you been working hard?
englishGrammar.explanation: You look tired 表示現在看起來很累，重點是之前持續工作的活動及其造成的現在結果。

englishGrammar.rule: 現在完成進行式（過程強調）
englishGrammar.wrong: You look as if you have cried.
englishGrammar.correct: You look as if you have been crying.
englishGrammar.explanation: 句子從現在的外表推測對方之前一直在哭，重點是活動過程，而不是哭這件事是否完成。

englishGrammar.rule: 現在完成式（has gone 用法）
englishGrammar.wrong: Where has Lisa been going?
englishGrammar.correct: Where has Lisa gone?
englishGrammar.explanation: has gone 表示 Lisa 已經去了某處，目前不在這裡；has been going 則表示她最近一直往某處去，意思不同。

englishGrammar.wrong: I have been having this book since I was a child.
englishGrammar.correct: I have had this book since I was a child.
englishGrammar.explanation: have 在此表示擁有。即使有 since，仍應使用現在完成式，而不是現在完成進行式。

englishGrammar.rule: 副詞用法（ever 的使用時機）
englishGrammar.wrong: Have you ever seen my phone?
englishGrammar.correct: Have you seen my phone?
englishGrammar.explanation: ever 表示人生經驗中的「曾經」。尋找眼前遺失的特定手機時，只需要問對方是否看見過它。

englishGrammar.wrong: I have read the book, but I haven’t finished it yet.
englishGrammar.correct: I have been reading the book, but I haven’t finished it yet.
englishGrammar.explanation: 尚未讀完，因此重點是持續進行的閱讀活動，應使用 have been reading。

englishGrammar.wrong: I have been reading the book, so you can have it back now.
englishGrammar.correct: I have read the book, so you can have it back now.
englishGrammar.explanation: 書現在可以歸還，表示已經讀完，重點是完成結果，因此使用 have read。

englishGrammar.rule: 一般現在式與現在完成式
englishGrammar.wrong: She has been married to a German guy.
englishGrammar.correct: She is married to a German guy.
englishGrammar.explanation: 題目只問 Amy 現在是否已婚，沒有強調結婚多久，因此使用 is married。若有時間長度，才可說 She has been married for ten years。

englishGrammar.rule: 一般現在式與現在完成式
englishGrammar.wrong: He has lived in Milan.
englishGrammar.correct: He lives in Milan.
englishGrammar.explanation: 句子只是在補充 Martin 現在住在米蘭。若要使用 has lived，通常需要 for 或 since 等時間資訊。

englishGrammar.wrong: I haven’t went to the cinema for ages.
englishGrammar.correct: I haven’t been to the cinema for ages.
englishGrammar.explanation: went 是一般過去式，不能放在 have 後面。haven’t been to 表示已經很久沒有去過某地。

englishGrammar.wrong: Have you always been living in Chicago?
englishGrammar.correct: Have you always lived in Chicago?
englishGrammar.explanation: always 強調整段期間一貫不變的狀態，課本通常使用現在完成式 have always lived。

englishGrammar.wrong: I just wake up.
englishGrammar.correct: I just woke up.
englishGrammar.explanation: 起床的動作已經完成，所以不能使用現在式 wake。英式英文也可以說 I've just woken up.

englishGrammar.wrong: I buy this book.
englishGrammar.correct: I bought this book.
englishGrammar.explanation: 買書是已經發生的動作，因此 buy 要改成過去式 bought。

englishGrammar.wrong: I always will went into that shop.
englishGrammar.correct: I will always go into that shop.
englishGrammar.explanation: will 後使用原形 go，不能使用過去式 went。頻率副詞 always 通常放在 will 後面。

englishGrammar.wrong: It's first time.
englishGrammar.correct: It's the first time.
englishGrammar.explanation: 表示「這是第一次」時，固定說法是 It's the first time.

englishGrammar.rule: everyone 視為單數，動詞需用第三人稱單數
englishGrammar.wrong: I think everyone go to different places by themselves.
englishGrammar.correct: I think everyone goes to different places by themselves.
englishGrammar.explanation: everyone 雖然代表許多人，但文法上是單數，因此動詞要使用 goes。

englishGrammar.rule: 數字 three 後面需接複數名詞與複數動詞
englishGrammar.wrong: This three color is convenient to combine with different clothes.
englishGrammar.correct: These three colours are easy to match with different clothes.
englishGrammar.explanation: three colours 是複數，因此指示代名詞、名詞與動詞都要使用複數（these、colours、are）。衣服顏色搭配通常使用 match with。

englishGrammar.rule: many 後面應接可數名詞複數
englishGrammar.wrong: It has many size.
englishGrammar.correct: It comes in many sizes.
englishGrammar.explanation: size 應改為複數 sizes。描述衣服有多種尺寸時，習慣使用 comes in many sizes。

englishGrammar.rule: 避免直接按中文直譯，應使用清楚的主動詞結構與連接詞
englishGrammar.wrong: I think it's right need to more people use bicycle.
englishGrammar.correct: I think more people should cycle because it is better for the environment.
englishGrammar.explanation: 原句缺少清楚的主詞與動詞結構。建議使用 should 表達「應該」，並用 because 補充原因。

englishGrammar.wrong: I have some technical to cut down my time.
englishGrammar.correct: I have learned some techniques to reduce my reading time.
englishGrammar.explanation: technical 是形容詞；表示方法或技巧時要使用名詞 techniques。reduce my reading time 比 cut down my time 更清楚。

englishGrammar.wrong: Experiencing it yourself is different for the information on the internet.
englishGrammar.correct: Experiencing a place yourself is different from seeing it online.
englishGrammar.explanation: 固定搭配是 different from。seeing it online 也比 information on the internet 更符合原本想表達的意思。

englishGrammar.wrong: I think it's different experience for visit some places already famous.
englishGrammar.correct: I think visiting a less well-known place can be a completely different experience.
englishGrammar.explanation: for 後不能直接接動詞原形 visit。原回答也把 less well-known 說成 already famous，因此要先確認題目意思再回答。

englishGrammar.wrong: I haven’t seen him for last week.
englishGrammar.correct: I haven’t seen him since last week.
englishGrammar.explanation: last week 在這裡表示「從上週開始」，屬於起始時間點，因此使用 since。若是一段時間，才說 for a week。

englishGrammar.wrong: How long has Anna been in London? — Last week.
englishGrammar.correct: When did Anna arrive in London? — Last week.
englishGrammar.explanation: Last week 回答的是抵達的時間，不是持續時間，因此問句應使用 When 加一般過去式。

englishGrammar.wrong: He has been being ill since Sunday.
englishGrammar.correct: He has been ill since Sunday.
englishGrammar.explanation: ill 是形容詞，be ill 表示「生病的狀態」。現在完成式是 has been ill，不需要再加入 being。

englishGrammar.wrong: She got married for a year ago.
englishGrammar.correct: She got married a year ago.
englishGrammar.explanation: a year ago 已經完整表示「一年前」，不能再加 for。若使用 for，應改成 She has been married for a year.

englishGrammar.rule: 現在完成式與一般過去式
englishGrammar.wrong: I’ve been working there for six months ago.
englishGrammar.correct: I’ve been working there for six months.
englishGrammar.explanation: for six months 表示工作持續了六個月，搭配現在完成進行式。也可以改成一般過去式：I started working there six months ago.

englishGrammar.wrong: Kate started learning Japanese long time ago.
englishGrammar.correct: Kate started learning Japanese a long time ago.
englishGrammar.explanation: 表示「很久以前」時，固定使用 a long time ago。

englishGrammar.wrong: I haven’t rode a bike for ages.
englishGrammar.correct: I haven’t ridden a bike for ages.
englishGrammar.explanation: ride 的三態是 ride–rode–ridden。rode 是過去式；ridden 才是可以接在 have/has 後面的過去分詞。

englishGrammar.wrong: It’s five years since I haven’t had a holiday.
englishGrammar.correct: It’s five years since I last had a holiday.
englishGrammar.explanation: since 後面要描述上一次事件發生的時間，因此使用一般過去式 had。last 可清楚表達「上一次」。

wordRoots.meaning: 球莖；膨脹物；圓形突起物
wordRoots.origin: 源自拉丁文 bulbus (意指「洋蔥，球莖」)，而 bulbus 又來自希臘文 bolbos (同樣指「洋蔥，球莖」)。這些詞語被認為最終源於原始印歐語詞根 *bhel- (意指「吹氣，膨脹」)。

examples.meaning: 這個字在英文中本身就是一個不可再分的字根，源自拉丁文「洋蔥」或「膨脹物」的意思。它不包含常見的英文前綴或後綴。
球莖狀的；膨脹的；圓胖的
球；球狀物 (與 bulb 最終共享「膨脹」的印歐語根)
氣球；熱氣球 (與 bulb 最終共享「膨脹」的印歐語根)

wordRoots.ieltsTip: 「Bulb」及其相關概念（如「膨脹」、「圓形」）常用於描述科學、地理或技術文章中的物體形狀或構造，例如在生物學中描述植物部分 (plant bulbs)、在物理學中描述燈泡 (light bulbs)。理解其「膨脹、圓形」的核心意義，有助於理解相關描述性詞彙，這在雅思閱讀和寫作的學術文本中很常見。
這是一個在學術文章和聽力中常見的正式詞彙，了解其「禁止、宣告非法」的含義以及與 prescribe (規定、開藥) 的區別，對雅思閱讀和寫作非常重要。

wordRoots.note: 這個字根源於古法語 'garder'，在英語中常以 -ward 或 -guard 的形式出現。｜「re-」表示「回」，「ward」源自「看顧、留意」之意，加上「-ing」形成形容詞，表示某件事是「值得你付出努力去獲得回報的」，因此是有益處的。

examples.meaning: 有益的，值得的，有報酬的
